Subject: Request: EU deployment footprint + evidence for RFP section 3.2

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Novamed’s procurement team has started the formal RFP review. Section 3.2 asks for a detailed statement of where customer data is stored and processed for EU customers, plus evidence that (a) no customer data is routed outside the EU without explicit consent, and (b) fallback routing behavior in cross-region outage scenarios.

Specifically we need:
- A short commitment letter that we can attach to the bid stating that for EU-bound workloads, data at rest and processing remain within EU data centers by default.
- Network/topology diagrams and a short operational note describing automated fallback paths (if any), and how KV cache or replication behaves during failover.
- Any SOC/attestation artifacts or pointer where we can retrieve them.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide these items and a single-pack PDF we can upload to the portal? Deadline for the RFP appendix is Friday, Nov 5.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement — Novamed Health
elena.rossi@novamed.it

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.it>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: EU deployment footprint + evidence for RFP section 3.2

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list and the deadline. We can provide everything you requested. Summary below and I will attach a consolidated evidence pack for upload:

1) Residency commitment: Redwood will by default store and process customer data for EU customers in EU-hosted regions (EU West and EU Central). We will provide a signed commitment letter for your bid (attached).

2) Network / topology evidence: included diagrams showing tenant isolation, VPC peering patterns for Private deployments, and the routing policy that enforces EU-only egress for pinned workloads.

3) Fallback behavior: our production routing policy supports regional failover to compatible model variants; for residency-sensitive workloads we offer two options:
   - Strict-residency mode: fail open is disabled. If EU capacity is unavailable, requests are queued or return a 503 rather than cross-border failover.
   - Permissive failover (opt-in): will route to other regions with explicit customer consent — we log and surface any cross-border events in the Console and audit logs.

4) Attestations & evidence pointers: SOC 2 Type II summary and the EU audit annex are available; we will include a pointer link and the excerpt relevant to data locality.

I’ve looped in Ben Carter (Product Ops) and Laura Bennett (Legal/Privacy) to confirm the wording and include the sworn commitment letter. Expect the consolidated PDF and network diagram by Monday, Nov 2. If Novamed needs earlier, we can prioritize.

Best regards,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
